key_insight: LeVo 2 improves full-length song generation by splitting the problem into hierarchical semantic planning, track-specific refinement, and diffusion-based waveform reconstruction.
engineering_relevance: The paper offers a practical training-and-architecture recipe for controllable audio generation systems that must balance long-range coherence, lyric alignment, and detailed timbre quality.
method: LeLM first predicts mixed tokens for global musical planning, then predicts vocal and accompaniment tokens in parallel for track-level refinement.
A Music Codec diffusion model reconstructs the final full-length waveform from the hierarchical representation.
Progressive post-training uses SFT, large-scale offline DPO, and closed-loop semi-online DPO, guided by musicality-tier pretraining labels and a modular track-specific extension.
evidence_signal: Expert listening tests and objective evaluations show improvements over open-source baselines across six subjective dimensions, with performance approaching leading commercial systems on several metrics.
watch_item: The multi-stage training pipeline is complex and may be sensitive to data quality, reward design, and optimization instability when scaling or reproducing.
paper_title: LeVo 2: Stable and Melodious Song Generation via Hierarchical Representation Modeling and Progressive Post-Training
